conviction_note: easyJet is a target under a recommended 715p cash offer from Apollo (Eagle Bidco), approved by shareholders on 11 Nov 2026 and expected to close before end-Q1 2027. The stock is a merger-arb instrument pinned at 688-690p (20d realised vol 6.3% annualised, about 0.4% a day), so FY26 numbers cannot reprice it. Only news on the outstanding regulatory conditions could, and nothing sourced says which way that will go. Every finding is 0 and the sum is 0. The scaled number is p_up 50 on an abs_move of 0.8%. That is far below the 3% European base and deliberately so: the base rates were measured on standalone names, and a capped cash offer is the documented exception ('in a live bid, results are noise').

already_public.what: Recommended cash acquisition at 715p per share by Eagle Bidco (Apollo funds), Rule 2.7 announcement, with an unlisted rollover alternative; any dividend declared before the Effective Date reduces the consideration by the same amount

new_in_release.expect: FY26 headline PBT well below FY25's £665m given the H1 loss and the Q3 decline. Irrelevant to a stock capped by a 715p cash offer.
An FY27 outlook may be given or withheld in an offer period. Either way it does not reprice a fixed cash offer except through deal-break odds, which are negligible from earnings.
Value-neutral. Any dividend declared reduces the 715p consideration pound for pound (Rule 2.7 para 3).

Unknown, and the only line that can move the stock: commentary on the outstanding aviation, ownership-and-control, merger-control and FDI conditions, and the timetable to sanction. 'All on track for end-Q1 2027' is roughly flat to slightly up as the 3.9% spread accretes. A slip or a regulatory obstacle could cost 1-3%.

session_check: bmo. Every easyJet results RNS on Investegate is stamped 07:00 London: Final Results 25 Nov 2025 07:00, 28 Nov 2023 07:00, Half-year Report 21 May 2026 07:00 (https://www.investegate.co.uk/company/EZJ). The date fits cadence (25 Nov 2025, 28 Nov 2023, 29 Nov 2022) and the vendor row. The event is unconfirmed but not disproved, and my numbers would be the same without it.

findings.finding: easyJet is in an offer period under a recommended 715p cash scheme (Apollo/Eagle Bidco). Shareholders approved it on 11 Nov 2026 (97.07% at the Court Meeting) and completion is expected before end-Q1 2027, so the stock (688.42p, 3.86% gross spread) trades on deal completion, not on FY26 earnings.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Since the 6 Aug 2026 firm offer the stock has held 666-691p. Scheme document day (15 Oct) +1.0%, 5 Nov +1.3% on 20m shares, the meeting result (11 Nov) -0.2%. The baseline's 2.26% median reaction is from pre-offer prints and its dates are misaligned with the RNS record (e.g. 2025-11-17 used against the real 25 Nov 2025 Final Results).
findings.why_not_priced: It is fully priced, which is why it is sized 0. The finding is that the print is not the event the vendor calendar thinks it is. If the market were treating results as live, the stock would not have sat within 666-691p for three months on a 0.4% daily realised vol.

findings.finding: Under the Rule 2.7 terms, any FY26 dividend declared in the results lets Bidco cut the 715p consideration by the same amount, so the dividend line is value-neutral.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FY25 proposed a 13.2p dividend at 20% payout, but under a fixed offer there is no precedent on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Priced by construction: the reduction mechanism is in the offer terms. Sized 0.

findings.finding: Regulatory conditions are still outstanding. The scheme document was delayed for 'continuing constructive engagement with the relevant aviation regulators', EU persons held only 35.07% of the shares at the meeting, and the sanction hearing is unset. Any update in the results release on these conditions is the only line that can move the stock, and its sign is unsourced.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Regulatory and timetable news has moved this name about 1% at most since the offer (scheme document day +1.0%). There is no precedent of a regulatory setback.
findings.why_not_priced: The risk is priced in the 3.86% spread (about 11-12% annualised to a late-March close, wide for a voted deal). I have nothing saying whether the release will narrow or widen it, so it is sized 0, with an asymmetric range because a slip costs more than confirmation gains.
findings.independence: The result of meeting confirms the remaining conditions and the EU ownership share: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/mfn/easyjet--ezj/result-of-meeting/9870224

findings.finding: Disclosed net short is 1.42% and building (+0.22pp to 2026-11-20) in a stock capped by a cash offer. That is neither squeeze fuel nor an informed negative signal on earnings.
findings.why_not_priced: Sized 0. With upside capped at 715p a squeeze cannot run above the offer, and the baseline lean of +0.35 should be read as noise here.

findings.finding: The competing-bid tail is thin. Castlelake (last indication 690p) made a Rule 2.8 no-offer statement on 6 Aug 2026, and the Haji-Ioannou concert party's 15.31% irrevocable stays binding unless a rival offer pays more than a 9% premium (above about 779p), so a bump inside a one-session window is remote.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Apollo/Castlelake contest ran June-August 2026, before the firm offer. Nothing since.
findings.why_not_priced: Priced: the stock trades below the offer, not above it, which is what no expected bump looks like. Sized 0.
findings.independence: Irrevocable terms in the Rule 2.7 announcement https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/easyjet--ezj/offer-for-easyjet-plc/9709252

outside_window.finding: Satisfaction of the regulatory conditions, the sanction hearing and the Effective Date (expected before end-Q1 2027). The 3.86% spread closes only then.

baseline_tension: The baseline lean (+0.35, mostly the short-squeeze term) and the flat run-up (+1.24% over 20d) assume a free-floating stock. What I found says the price is anchored by a 715p cash offer, so the lean is mis-specified here rather than contradicted, and the hunt agrees with the flat tape.
language_note: nothing the English sources did not already carry. The decisive facts (offer, vote result, dividend clause, Castlelake 2.8 statement) are all RNS documents on Investegate that the international wires also reported; the domestic RNS archive was simply the fastest primary route to them.
lessons_applied: 'In a live bid, results are noise ... the offer is the finding' confirmed the draft's frame and prompted one added finding: the Castlelake Rule 2.8 statement and the irrevocable threshold, which bound the competing-offer tail. Sized 0, so impact_sum is unchanged at 0.

'Too small about the move / understatement' raised abs_move_pct from 0.6 to 0.8 to leave room for a regulatory-timetable surprise in the release. It was not taken to the 3% base, because that base was measured on standalone names and a capped cash offer is the exception the same file names. p_up unchanged at 50.
